title: ToolResult
description: The normalized outcome of a ToolCall. Every capability reports success, failure, denial and cancellation in this one shape so TurnExecutor and the M5 degradation logic can react without knowing which capability ran.

compatibility.notes: `trust_of_output` is required and is the subtle one: a tool result is content of UNKNOWN provenance and must degrade the turn's trust when it enters context. Making it optional would silently reopen the injection path that ADR-0012 closes — a tool that fetches a web page would otherwise return attacker text at whatever trust the turn already had. Adding an `outcome` value is MAJOR: consumers switch exhaustively on it and an unrecognised outcome must never fall through to 'treat as success'.

outcome.description: `denied` is a Policy Engine refusal and is a NORMAL outcome — the brain should be told plainly so it can explain, not retry. `rolled_back` means a write was cancelled mid-flight and undone (ADR-0025).

content.description: Result payload on success. Shape per the tool's output_schema. MUST NOT contain raw binary — a tool returning media returns a reference, never inline bytes (ADR-0006).

trust_of_output.description: Trust level this result carries INTO the turn. Almost always `tool_result` or lower. A tool that reads a file or fetches a URL MUST report `external_content` — the turn's effective trust then drops to the minimum, and write tools become unreachable for the rest of the turn. This single field is what stops content laundering through a tool call.

side_effect_applied.description: What actually happened, which may differ from what was declared if the tool short-circuited. Recorded for audit.

truncated.description: Content was cut to fit the context budget. The brain must be told, or it will reason confidently about a partial answer.

error.message: This action needs to come from you directly. I read it from a file, so I won't act on it.
error.detail: tool requires operator; effective turn trust external_content
